title: Doxorubicin for soft tissue sarcoma
context_label: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
indication_text: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
purpose: The aim is usually to control advanced sarcoma, reduce cancer-related symptoms or slow growth. Your consultant explains the realistic goal for your own tumour and circumstances.
schedule_summary: NCCP 00500 gives doxorubicin 75 mg/m² on day 1 of a 21-day cycle, usually for 3–6 cycles. The source allows consideration of 60 mg/m² in people over 70; the prescribed dose and number of cycles are individual decisions.
administration_text: Doxorubicin is given intravenously on day 1 by trained staff through suitable venous access. Blood tests, review, anti-sickness medicines and observation make the whole visit longer than the injection itself.
monitoring_summary: Use the test-specific schedule below. Safety tests, symptom checks and scans serve different purposes.

agents.name: Doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Damages DNA and interferes with repair
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care.
agents.watch: Report breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations or ankle swelling promptly. Tell the nurse immediately about pain or burning at the infusion site. Red urine can occur briefly after the dose; painful urination, clots or persistent redness need assessment.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth ulcers, hair loss and fatigue
Heart muscle damage or rhythm problems; heart damage may appear later and can be permanent
Severe tissue injury if the medicine leaks outside the vein
Fertility and pregnancy harm; rare later leukaemia or other blood cancers

anatomy: Soreness, nausea or vomiting can reduce eating and drinking. Use the prescribed anti-sickness plan and ask early for help.
Heart effects can occur during treatment or later. Previous anthracycline doses matter. Report new breathlessness, ankle swelling, chest pain or palpitations.
Liver blood tests help guide safe treatment. New jaundice or severe upper abdominal pain needs urgent assessment.
Urine may briefly look red after treatment. Pain, clots or persistent redness is not assumed to be harmless and needs assessment.
Low blood counts can cause infection, anaemia or bleeding. Fever, shaking chills or sudden illness needs immediate contact.
Constipation or diarrhoea can follow treatment or support medicines. Report persistent symptoms, severe pain or inability to drink.
Hair loss and skin changes may occur. Pain or burning where treatment enters the vein must be reported immediately.
Fatigue may persist between visits. Discuss fertility preservation and pregnancy precautions before treatment.

monitoring_schedule.note: Safety testing and cancer-response assessment have different purposes. Your plan may change after illness or a dose adjustment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check white cells for infection risk, haemoglobin for anaemia and platelets for bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before first treatment and before each cycle. Extra counts may be needed for symptoms or abnormal results.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check safe medicine handling and identify kidney or liver effects.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; repeat sooner for symptoms, abnormal results or clinical concerns.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart assessment and lifetime exposure
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess anthracycline-related heart risk and account for previous doxorubicin or related treatment.
monitoring_test_details.timing: electrocardiogram (ECG) before treatment. echocardiogram (heart ultrasound) (ECHO) or multigated acquisition (heart pumping) scan (MUGA) if over 65 or clinically indicated; the source baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (heart pumping measurement) (LVEF) criterion is at least 50%. Review cardiac symptoms and cumulative anthracycline exposure during treatment; further heart tests follow clinical risk or symptoms.

monitoring_test_details.label: Mouth and throat examination
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify soreness, infection or problems affecting nutrition.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting; review mouth symptoms during treatment and examine as indicated.

monitoring_test_details.label: Medicines and symptoms
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check interactions, treatment toxicity and whether support prescriptions are complete.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before treatment and at each treatment review; report new symptoms or medicine changes between visits.

monitoring_test_details.label: Cancer response and follow-up
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess cancer control separately from safety blood tests.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Your consultant sets the scan and clinical-review schedule according to the sarcoma and treatment aim.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: No separate routine drug premedication is specified by NCCP, but prescribed anti-sickness treatment is required. Review all medicines, prior anthracyclines, heart symptoms and pregnancy/fertility plans before starting. This is a high nausea/vomiting-risk treatment. Use one written prevention and rescue plan before and after treatment. Confirm any prescribed stomach protection and local mouth-care measures; do not add duplicate support courses.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses suitable intravenous access and explains line care. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, redness or swelling during an injection or drip. Do not wait for the visit to finish. If you have a port or PICC, agree dressing, flushing and removal arrangements.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding as directed. Your team must give written contraception and post-treatment precautions for every medicine, using current product information; the required duration may differ by medicine and between patients.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: A sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment, fitness and your priorities. Surgery and radiotherapy may help local control in selected circumstances; their role and timing are decided separately. Chemotherapy does not automatically replace an operation or radiotherapy. Supportive and palliative care can be used alongside cancer treatment to help symptoms and daily life.

items.title: General chemotherapy risks
items.text: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste change, diarrhoea or constipation; tiredness, hair and skin changes; infusion reactions and intravenous-line complications; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, rare later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. Risks differ between medicines and people. The medicine-specific section explains the main additional risks for this regimen.

evidence.title: GeDDiS: first-line chemotherapy in advanced soft tissue sarcoma
evidence.summary: In GeDDiS, first-line doxorubicin 75 mg/m² every three weeks was compared with gemcitabine 675 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 plus docetaxel 75 mg/m² on day 8. The combination did not improve progression-free or overall survival over doxorubicin in the study population.
evidence.intro: In GeDDiS, first-line doxorubicin 75 mg/m² every three weeks was compared with gemcitabine 675 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 plus docetaxel 75 mg/m² on day 8. The combination did not improve progression-free or overall survival over doxorubicin in the study population.
evidence.caveat: This trial informs a treatment discussion for previously untreated advanced soft tissue sarcoma. It does not predict an individual response, establish a benefit for every sarcoma subtype or determine later-line treatment.
evidence.interpretation: This trial informs a treatment discussion for previously untreated advanced soft tissue sarcoma. It does not predict an individual response, establish a benefit for every sarcoma subtype or determine later-line treatment.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Are blood tests the same as checking whether treatment works?
questions.a: No. Blood counts and organ tests mainly check safety. Your sarcoma team uses the clinical review and planned imaging to assess cancer control.
